schema.value: dict[str, str] mapping served prompt name to the journey id whose steps it renders; every value must be a journey the packaged snapshot records.

intent.value: Which served prompt walks which recorded journey: a prompt named here renders its steps from the journey record, so adding, removing or rewording a step in the model is the only way to change what the prompt says.

schema.value: dict[str, str] mapping served prompt name to the reason its flow is not one of the recorded journeys; together with PROMPT_JOURNEYS the keys are exactly the served prompts.

intent.value: Why each of the other served prompts is still authored rather than bound to a journey. Written down because 'this prompt is not bound' and 'somebody forgot to bind this prompt' look identical from outside, and only one of them is a decision.

expects.value: journey_id names a journey the packaged documentation snapshot records

forbids.value: Never invents a step, or a path for a journey the packaged documentation snapshot does not record.

guarantees.value: Returns the steps in walking order, every word of them read from the record; a journey this build does not record renders as nothing rather than as an invented path

intent.value: Renders one recorded journey as the numbered ladder a prompt teaches: each step's call, why it is taken and what a good result looks like, any approval it needs, then the named things that can go wrong and what to do about each

The steps themselves are NOT here — __JOURNEY_STEPS__ is where journey:mcp-authoring-loop renders in, from the record.

intent.value: The look-inward-first runtime fault journey: observed symptom, project_status runtime context, runbook, suspect and dependency-neighbor inspection, host evidence when needed, and a live-behavior probe that preserves durable state.

expects.value: project_root and module_name are non-empty; kind, when given, is a scaffold-recognized nerve kind

guarantees.value: Returns the rendered journey text with every placeholder marker substituted, its numbered steps identical to the ones journey:mcp-authoring-loop records

intent.value: Walks an agent through authoring one new module end to end, rendering the steps of journey:mcp-authoring-loop from the record rather than from a copy in the prompt text, wrapped in the framing the record does not carry: the golden rule, the survival card, the argument shapes, and the editing that happens between steps

guarantees.value: Returns the rendered journey text with the project root substituted

intent.value: Walks an agent through diagnosing and clearing check failures: group structured diagnostics by code, fix highest severity first via each remediation, re-check until clean

guarantees.value: Returns the rendered journey text with the project root substituted

intent.value: Walks an agent through migrating a pre-consolidation project: migrate_ext dry-run, present the plan, apply, rebuild, and check until clean

guarantees.value: Returns the look-inward-first diagnostic journey with the project root and observed fault substituted

intent.value: Guides an agent from an observed runtime fault through project_status, declared runtime/runbook context, suspect and dependency-neighbor inspection, host evidence when needed, and a state-preserving live behavior probe.

metadata.mcp_prompt_title: Send feedback to the s0ma team

intent.value: Walks an agent through carrying one piece of the user's own feedback to the s0ma team: identify it, confirm it is about s0ma when the user never said so, draft from evidence, prepare, show the exact feedback data and what redaction removed, submit only through the client's approval form, and relay the receipt or the saved draft

Release-gate verification (FR-DSL-6 coverage) that every journey prompt renders its embedded template with the client's arguments substituted and no placeholder marker left behind — the rendering nerves' guarantee, exercised on the built module pytest imports; the feedback journey additionally renders with its one argument absent, the case whose whole point is that the agent is told to ask rather than to invent; and the PROMPT_JOURNEYS binding is proved from the record, so a journey step edited in the model reaches the served prompt or turns this red.

fix_check_failures_prompt READS FIX_CHECK_FAILURES_TEMPLATE: journey prompt copy
migrate_project_prompt READS MIGRATE_PROJECT_TEMPLATE: journey prompt copy

intent.value: Says how one journey step is taken, in the words of the channel that takes it: a tool is called, a prompt is used, a command is run. Derived from the surface id's own class rather than from a table beside it, so a journey that grows a step on a new channel names that step rather than silently rendering a raw id.

Authoring and operational journey prompts for the s0ma MCP server: author a module, fix check failures, migrate a legacy project, diagnose an observed runtime fault from project self-knowledge before broad code search, or carry the user's own feedback about s0ma to the s0ma team through the prepare-review-approve path they control. A prompt whose flow IS a journey the documentation model records renders that journey's steps from the record instead of keeping a second copy of them in its text (PROMPT_JOURNEYS); each prompt whose flow is not a recorded journey stays authored and says why in PROMPT_WITHOUT_JOURNEY rather than leaving a reader to guess whether the binding was forgotten.
